text: In the beginning, God made everything: the sky, the trees, the flowers, and the birds.
Then He made the first man and woman, Adam and Eve.
God was with them in their garden home, Eden.
They loved being with Him, and He loved them.
Everything was perfect.
God gave Adam and Eve every tree in the garden to enjoy, except one.
“Do not eat from that tree,” God said. “If you do, you will die.”
Adam pointed to the tree so Eve would remember.
It was one simple rule from a Father who loved them.
One day, a sneaky serpent slid down beside Eve.
“Did God really say that?” he hissed.
“You won’t die! That fruit will make you like God!”
But the serpent was lying.
He wanted Eve to stop trusting God.
Eve looked at the fruit. It looked so good, so she took a bite.
Then she gave some to Adam, and he ate it too.
Uh-oh.
For the very first time, people had disobeyed God.
The Bible calls this sin.
And the serpent grinned. His trick had worked.
Sin changed everything. Now Adam and Eve felt afraid and ashamed.
God made them clothes from animal skins.
But to make them, innocent animals had to die.
But God also made them a promise.
One day, Someone would come to crush the serpent and open the way back home.
Then God sent them out of the garden, and an angel guarded the way back in.
Adam and Eve had children, and their children had children, all the way down to you and me.
Look at all these people!
Every one of them has sin marks, just like Adam and Eve.
The Bible says we have all sinned, and our sin keeps us far from God.
God gave us ten good rules, called the Ten Commandments.
Have you ever told a lie? Even once?
Have you ever taken something that wasn’t yours?
If so, that makes you a liar and a thief.
That doesn’t feel very good, does it?
And that’s only two of the ten!
Like Adam and Eve, we have all broken God’s law, and our sin leaves marks we can’t hide.
God’s law is like a mirror. It shows us our sin, but it can’t wash it away.
Sin locks us out of God’s home, just like Adam and Eve were locked out of the garden.
God is good and fair, so He can’t just pretend our sin never happened.
The Bible says that if we die with our sin, we will be punished in a place called hell, far away from God forever.
That is very bad news.
So how can we get rid of our sin?
We might try to scrub it off by being extra good, saying sorry, or going to church.
But no matter how hard we scrub, the marks won’t come off.
Being good tomorrow can’t erase the wrong things we did today.
Remember the animals that died to cover Adam and Eve?
Someone has to take our place too.
But who?
Here is the good news! That someone is Jesus, God’s own Son.
He was there in the garden with Adam and Eve, and He is the One God promised.
God loved the world so much that He sent Jesus to bring us home.
Jesus said, “I am the door. Whoever comes in through Me will be saved.”
That’s why people who know Jesus love to tell others, “Come and see! There is a way back to God!”
Jesus never sinned, not even once.
But He died on a cross in our place, like the animals that died for Adam and Eve.
All our sin was put on Him, and He took the punishment we deserved.
Jesus did this because He loves us.
Now everyone has a choice to make.
Some people say, “No thanks,” and walk away.
Others tell God, “I’m sorry for my sin. I believe Jesus died in my place. Please forgive me and save me!”
That means turning away from sin and trusting Jesus.
When we do, God takes our sin away and covers us with Jesus’ goodness.
Jesus loves you, and He lets you choose.
Three days after Jesus died, His friends found His tomb empty.
Jesus was alive again! He had beaten sin and death!
Everyone who trusts Him is as clean and white as snow.
The gate is open. Jesus has made a way back home!
One day, everyone who trusts Jesus will run through heaven’s open gates.
And Jesus will be right there, with His arms open wide.
The same Jesus who sent Adam and Eve out of the garden will welcome His children home.
You can still see the scars in His hands, the scars of His love.
And guess what?
God will make everything new: a new heaven and a new earth, even better than Eden!
Until that day, Jesus asks you to tell others the good news, so they can find the way back home too.

prayer.title: Would you like to follow Jesus?

steps.rest: to God that you have sinned, and say you are sorry.

prayer.prayer: “Dear God, I know I have sinned, and I am sorry. Thank You for sending Jesus to die for me and rise again. Please forgive me and make me clean. I want to follow You. In Jesus’ name, amen.”
prayer.note: Talk with a parent, pastor, or grown-up you trust about what you prayed.

grownups.title: For grown-ups
grownups.intro: Try these questions after reading together.
questions: What was the one rule God gave Adam and Eve? Why do you think He gave it?
Why couldn’t the children scrub their marks away?
What did Jesus do so we could come back to God?
How do we know Jesus is alive?
What does it mean to trust Jesus? Is that something you want to do?
Who is someone you could tell the good news to this week?

tract.tag: A true story from the Bible
panels: In the beginning, God created everything, and it was very good. He made the first people, Adam and Eve, in His own image, to know Him and to live with Him. God was with them in their garden home.

God gave them every tree in the garden to enjoy except one. “Do not eat from that tree,” He said. “If you do, you will die.” It was one simple command from a Father who loved them, and a real choice to trust Him.
Genesis 2:16–17
The serpent lied: “You won’t die! You’ll be like God!” Eve believed him and ate the fruit, and Adam ate it too. They chose their own way instead of God’s. The Bible calls this sin.
Genesis 3:1–6

Sin broke everything. Adam and Eve hid in shame, and animals had to die to cover them. They were sent out of the garden, away from God. But God promised that Someone would come to crush the serpent and open the way back home.
Genesis 3:15, 21–24
Every one of us has sinned, just like Adam and Eve. Have you ever lied? Taken what wasn’t yours? Hated someone in your heart? God’s law is like a mirror: it shows us that we have all broken it.
Romans 3:23; Exodus 20; Matthew 5:21–22

God is holy and just. He cannot ignore sin or pretend it never happened. The Bible says the penalty for sin is death, and after death comes judgment. If we die in our sin, we will be separated from God forever in hell.
Romans 6:23; Hebrews 9:27
We can’t fix this ourselves. Trying harder, saying sorry or going to church can’t wash sin away. Our good deeds can never cancel out the wrong we have done. Someone has to pay what we owe. But who?
Isaiah 64:6; Ephesians 2:8–9
Here is the good news! God loved the world so much that He sent His Son, Jesus, the One He promised in the garden. Jesus said, “I am the door. Whoever comes in through Me will be saved.”
John 3:16; John 10:9
Jesus never sinned, not even once. Yet He died on a cross in our place. All our sin was put on Him, and He took the punishment we deserved.
Isaiah 53:6; 2 Corinthians 5:21; 1 Peter 2:24

Now everyone has a choice. Some say “No thanks” and walk away. But when we turn from our sin and trust Jesus, God forgives us completely. He takes our sin away and covers us with Jesus’ perfect goodness.
Mark 1:15; Romans 10:9, 13; Isaiah 1:18
Three days after Jesus died, His tomb was empty. He had risen from the dead! Jesus defeated sin and death, and He is alive today. The way back home is open.
1 Corinthians 15:3–4
One day, everyone who trusts Jesus will run through heaven’s open gates. And Jesus Himself will be there to welcome them home, with His arms open wide.
John 14:2–3

God will make everything new: a new heaven and a new earth, with no more death, pain or tears. Until that day, Jesus sends everyone who follows Him to tell others, so they can find the way back home too.
Revelation 21:1–5; Matthew 28:19–20
tract.home: There is a way back home!
